extracted.intended_audience: consumers, journalists, public relations/marketing professionals, and others interested in evaluating health care news and messaging
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing the quality, accuracy, balance, and completeness of health care journalism, news releases, advertising, marketing and PR messages so consumers can make informed, shared decisions about health interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: improve public dialogue by helping consumers critically analyze claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission of HealthNewsReview.org is to improve the public dialogue about health care by helping consumers critically analyze claims about health care interventions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should aim to equip consumers to critically analyze claims about health interventions rather than to provide definitive medical advice or advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote shared decision-making supported by accurate, balanced, complete information
rubrics_metrics.description: Promoting the principles of shared decision-making reinforced by accurate, balanced and complete information about the tradeoffs involved in health care decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should look for whether coverage presents tradeoffs and information necessary for shared decision-making: accuracy of facts, balance of benefits vs harms, and completeness of relevant information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of review: include journalism, advertising, marketing, PR and other consumer-influencing messages
rubrics_metrics.description: HealthNewsReview.org evaluates health care journalism, advertising, marketing, public relations and other messages that may influence consumers and provides criteria that consumers can use to evaluate these messages themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rubric applies across multiple message types (news stories, news releases, ads, PR) and aims to provide consumer-facing criteria for evaluating influence and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence policy: no advertising accepted and no product promotion allowed in comments
rubrics_metrics.description: We don’t accept advertising and we won’t allow commenters to promote products on our site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear separation between funding and editorial content; do not allow commercial promotion to appear as user comments or sponsored content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence from funders
rubrics_metrics.description: No funder has ever had, nor will they ever have, any editorial control over the operation of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure and document that funders do not influence review outcomes or editorial decisions; transparency about funding sources should be provided while preserving editorial autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not a provider of medical advice or an advocacy organization
rubrics_metrics.description: We are not equipped to host a definitive forum on medical science. We don’t give medical advice. We are not an advocacy group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should avoid presenting themselves as medical advice or advocacy; the role is evaluative and informational for consumers, not prescriptive clinical guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical scope limits: cannot review everything
rubrics_metrics.description: We can’t review every story or every promotional message that we see. The tsunami of health care information each day is simply too overwhelming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge resource constraints when selecting items to review; prioritize items with high reach, potential consumer impact, or exemplar problems/strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of formal review criteria and star score (existence of structured rating system)
rubrics_metrics.description: Links and navigation point to 'How We Rate Stories', 'Review Criteria', and 'How is the Star Score Determined' indicating a structured set of review criteria and a star-scoring system is used to evaluate stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the site's defined review criteria and star-score methodology (see linked pages) when scoring individual items; the About page signals that evaluations are based on a consistent, documented rubric rather than ad hoc judgments.
